last_action: RAYEN HAS A SITE, AND THE APP LINKS TO IT (built and verified locally, NOT pushed). /about is the landing page, /guides holds three guides, /privacy is the policy: plain static HTML and one shared site.css in rayen-web/public/, no script, no build, in the manner of Alchemilla's site, reusing the app's own palette and type. The guides turn the survey into pages: how to keep track of when you water your plants, install and back up, and the story of why Rayen is a web app (from D13). SiteLinks (About, Privacy, Source) is in the Backup sheet and takes the hint's row on the empty-garden screen. npm run check:site is a new gate in RUN_TEST.sh and CI: links, titles, descriptions, canonicals, image alt and size, no scripts, sitemap parity. KEYWORD PLANNER IS BLOCKED ON GOOGLE: gum is signed in to Ads and a call reaches Google, which refuses it ('not allowed for explorer access'); the branding check must pass after its 24-hour wait, then Basic access must be granted. ALSO TODAY: SEO-SURVEY.md, listing drafts for Product Hunt and AlternativeTo, screenshots in marketing-assets/. EARLIER: OFFLINE IS CONFIRMED ON THE PHONE, AND THE HEADER IS OUT FROM UNDER iOS'S BLUR. 2026-11-13: the installed app opens in airplane mode with the garden and its type intact, which closes the service worker — the desk check (production build, real headers, server killed) could not stand in for WebKit standalone. The first true standalone install also showed the wordmark and both header buttons smeared, worst at their upper edges. Nothing in the app blurs them: since iOS 26 the system fades and blurs whatever a web app draws beneath the status bar, and this page runs full-bleed under a translucent one, so the header began exactly at the top of that strip. No CSS turns it off, so in the installed app the header sits 44px lower (the fade measured about 37px off a screenshot), scoped to display-mode: standalone and @supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none) so Safari and desktop are untouched. Confirmed on the phone. It never showed before because earlier phone screenshots had a browser bar above the page. RAYEN OPENS WITHOUT A NETWORK. A hand-written service worker, no dependency, emitted by offline.plugin.ts at build time with the hashed bundle list baked in — a browser only reinstalls a worker whose bytes changed, so a new deploy is a new worker, which fetches a complete copy of the app before replacing the old one. THREE RULES: pages network-first and never written back to the cache (a fresh page may name bundles the installed worker never fetched), bundles cache-first (their names carry a hash), fonts kept as they pass through in a cache that survives deploys. THE FONTS WERE THE HARD PART, because they come from Google and cannot be in the build list: a worker's own fetches answer to connect-src, so the two font hosts were added there; the stylesheet links gained crossorigin, since an opaque response cannot be checked before it is kept; and on a first visit the page has fetched its fonts before any worker exists, so it asks again on controllerchange. CHECKED AT A DESK against a production build with vercel.json's exact headers: a true first visit, then the server killed — both pages opened with the garden and all four faces intact, and a rebuild replaced the old cache. Eight tests run the worker's real source against a fake browser; breaking a rule fails one. KNOWN LIMIT: /grid asks for a different font stylesheet than the deck, so offline it falls back to system type until opened once online. Unifying the two links was rejected for now because the deck has one font-weight: 600 that currently renders from the 500 face, so the superset link would change how it looks. Earlier the same day: the move to rayen-garden.vercel.app, the storage keys renamed with it, the restore confirmed on the phone, juniper-design/ renamed to rayen-design/, and the stale CI billing blocker removed.

blockers.description: Keyword Planner is blocked on Google, not on code. The Google Auth branding check asked for a 24-hour wait after ownership was proved (2026-11-13) and must pass before Basic access can be requested; Explorer access is refused for Keyword Planner. Without ad spend the numbers may be broad ranges even then.

Rayen is unvalidated by real use. The deck has been exercised hard but against a demo garden over two days. Whether a fanned deck is the right way to meet eight plants every morning, and whether the ramp reads at a glance, are questions only real plants over real weeks answer.
Rayen has no reminders at all. A deliberate bet (D13) that the deck is itself the reminder, and the only thing that settles it is whether use happens anyway.
